To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the problem of planning manipulation strategies for sliding workpieces can be solved by using a search technique based on elementary manipulative operations, (2) the search space of the problem can be reduced significantly by applying a set of rules that restrict the search to a set of feasible strategies, and (3) a new representation of the problem is introduced which allows the use of a search technique that has been successfully applied to other problems, namely the problem of planning a path in a graph.

(1) we have demonstrated a general approach for planning manipulation strategies for sliding workpieces, (2) the approach is based on the concept of configuration map which maps the configuration of a workpiece to all possible outcomes, and (3) the concept of configuration mapping has been applied to design a class of passive part feeders.

(1) we can automatically design passive parts feeders that work in the presence of uncertainty; (2) we can automatically find the most robust feeder design for a given set of parts and a given conveyor belt.

the design and control of robotic systems that manipulate objects which slide on their work surfaces.
the automated planning of strategies for robotic manipulation of objects that slide on their work surfaces.
the automated design of robotic manipulation systems for workpieces which are able to slide on the work surface.
